correctness.rationale: The proof verifies normalizations, univalence and positive real parts on the full stated range. A pointwise Möbius inequality and Rouché yield exact logarithmic inradius. An exact positive-coefficient radial maximum, the Lambert inversion, and a canonical starlike extremal give sharp necessary and sufficient dilation for every real q in range; the endpoint and singular asymptotic are derived. Numeric checks are supplemental.

originality.rationale: A May 2026 apple-like coefficient study supplies the endpoint generator but the inspected sections do not state the two-way parameter inclusion law. The fully examined public generator catalog and 702 directed-radius records of the 2026 Geometric Function Atlas omit the apple-like endpoint and every nonzero-power exponential-apple interpolant. Publisher access limits prevent complete elimination of overlapping unpublished or inaccessible work.

value.rationale: Sharp directed inclusion is an established natural invariant, with a recent 2026 atlas devoted to such questions; the May 2026 apple-like function is the previously studied endpoint of this family. Exact reciprocal containment versus one-way Lambert-W loss, the exact inradius, and the q log(1/q) boundary singularity identify nontrivial structural asymmetry for a full continuous interpolation, not arbitrary slices or an unsupported numerical improvement.
